newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - INDIAN NEWSPAPERS - AUGUST 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - INDIAN NEWSPAPERS - AUGUST 11.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail: biznis@giasdl01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
SEVEN KESRI LOYALISTS IN CONGRESS WORKING COMMITTEE

Seven candidates from the panel of Congress party President Sitaram Kesri were elected to the Congress Working Committee by the All India Congress Committee. They are Ahmed Patel, Jitendra Prasada, Madhavrao Scindia, Pranab Mukherjee, Tariq Anwar and R.K. Dhawan. The surprise winners were Arjun Singh, Ghulam Nabi Azad and Sharad Pawar, who were not among Kesri's favourites. The election to fill 10 of the 20 posts was held on Sunday. Kesri promised to rectify a nonrepresentation of low castes other weaker sections in the Working Committee by nominating leaders belonging to these categories to the remaining posts.
The Economic Times
SOPS FOR EXPORT UNITS IN THE OFFING

The government is planning to give major concessions to export-oriented units to boost sagging exports, Commerce Minister B.B. Ramaiah said. This could include allowing longer working hours in export-oriented units, giving soft credits, a single window clearance for the approval of such units and reducing the number of bonds to be filled by these units. To increase exports, the government will have to prioritise its areas of operation and concentrate on select areas for export growth.
RESERVE BANK UNDECIDED ON REMOVING FORWARD COVER BAN

Fear and a sharp division of opinion may force the Reserve Bank to delay lifting the forward cover ban on foreign institutional investors. Some Reserve Bank of India (RBI) officials are in favour of freeing the ban while others feel there is need to be cautious because of recent turbulence in the Asian currency markets, sources said. The point of dispute is that any profit booked by foreign institutional investors as a result of booking forward covers may be repatriable. A section in the RBI feels that the rupee could come under pressure if foreign institutional investors were allowed to book forward covers.
TATA GROUP RAISES STAKE IN READERS DIGEST

The Tata group substantially raised its holding in RDI Print and Publishing, the publisher of Readers Digest. The Tatas bought the stakes of former Tata Steel chief Russi Mody and Aditya Kashyap. There is now speculation that the Tatas are considering using RDI Print as a platform to enter the media business. The Tata companies now hold about 78 percent of RDI's equity capital (2,32,640 shares). This shareholding is distributed between Titan Industries, Questar Investments and Titan Holdings.
Financial Express
RESERVE BANK SAYS NO TO LENDING BELOW PRIME RATE

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) turned down a proposal by the Bank of Baroda to lend below the prime lending rate. The RBI instead directed all commercial banks which want to lend below the prime lending rate to aggressively fund corporates by subscribing to their commercial paper issues. Currently most blue chip companies are raising money by issuing commercial paper at rates between nine and 12 percent. Bank of Baroda Managing Director K. Kannan said the bank wanted to do away with the concept of prime lending rate as very few corporates were able to access funds at this rate.
ITOCHU PLANS JOINT VENTURE WITH INDIAN COMPANY

Itochu Corporation of Japan has proposed setting up a 50:50 joint venture with the Delhi-based Ansal group for taking up dealership of Honda cars in India. Sources said Itochu would invest through its subsidiary Automobile Investment (Mauritius) which would subscribe in the equity of the proposed joint venture company to be called Capital Cars. Itochu has proposed a fee of 0.5 percent of the turnover of the joint venture company, up to a maximum of $200,000 a year for an initial period of seven years. The company plans to become operational by March 1998.
Business Standard
300 ITEMS TO BE REMOVED FROM RESTRICTED NEGATIVE LIST

The Commerce Ministry is likely to shift around 300 items from the restricted and negative lists to the open general licence list. Ministry sources said the move is expected towards the end of this month as part of a plan to ease quantitative restrictions on imports. It is likely to boost the premium on the special import licence which was hovering around 11.5 percent to 12 percent. Commerce Minister B.B. Ramaiah said India could not agree to phase out all import curbs in less than six years. Ministry sources said India will stick to her initial offer at the consultations to be held under the World Trade Organisation's dispute settlement body next month.
BOURSE REGULATOR PLANS ELECTRONIC SHARE ALLOTMENT

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is planning to institute an electronic allotment procedure which will enable an issuer to get his money within 10 days of the close of the issue. The procedure was proposed by the National bourse and Over the Counter Exchange. Both have a nation-wide network of brokers. SEBI's board on Tuesday will discuss slashing the allotment period and a panel report that suggested the introduction of a revised carryforward system. It is also likely to discuss a plan to revamp the system of primary issue marketing.
The Observer
INFLATION RATE FALLS TO 4.02 PERCENT

The annual rate of inflation based on the Wholesale Price Index fell to 4.02 percent during the week ended July 26. It was at 6.31 percent in the corresponding week last year. The rate of inflation calculated on a point-to-point basis fell by 0.17 percentage points from 4.19 percent to 4.02 percent. While the official Wholesale Price Index for all commodities (base 1981-82 100) rose marginally by 0.2 percent to 325.9 (provisional) during the week as against 325.4 (provisional) the week before.
STATE BANK ACT TO BE AMENDED

The Finance Ministry is amending the State Bank of India (SBI) Act and the SBI Subsidiary Act to facilitate the SBI to dilute its equity in its associate banks. The SBI will be allowed to dilute its stake in its subsidiary banks through public offerings once the acts are amended. According to SBI officials, the bank is planning to lower its stake in three of its subsidiaries, namely the State Bank of Jaipur and Bikaner, the State Bank of Patiala and the State Bank of Travancore.
